Done. The pruned 12-layer checkpoint is at `out/T1/model.safetensors` and passed both the built-in checks and an independent bit-exact comparison on the first execution.

**What I did**

- Wrote `out/T1/solution.py`, a plain script on safetensors and torch. It loads both input shards through the index file, drops blocks 2, 6, 10 and 14, and writes survivors into a fresh dict via a single old-to-new index map, so no rename order can collide.
- The script enforces the required checks before writing: no block index 12 or higher remains, indices are exactly 0..11 with 7 tensors each, 12 q_proj tensors, and 86 tensors total. It also verifies each survivor shares storage, shape and dtype with its source, writes to a temporary path, renames on success, and reloads the file to confirm the key set.
- Ran an independent check that every output tensor is bit-exact against its source block. It passed, all float32.
- Wrote `out/T1/REPORT.md` with the self-report fields. Executions: 1, no failures. Tools used: safetensors 0.5.3 and torch 2.14.0. mergekit and torch-state-bridge were considered but a short script was easier to make fail-loud and to verify.
